preconditions.description: The input contains a single integer k within the range [1, 10^9].

postconditions.description: The first line of output is an integer n representing the number of vertices, where 2 <= n <= 1000.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line) == n and all(c in 'NY' for c in line) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The remaining lines form an n x n adjacency matrix where each character is either 'N' or 'Y'.
The graph is simple: no self-loops exist (diagonal elements are 'N').

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.strip().splitlines()[i+1][j] == stdout.strip().splitlines()[j+1][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
postconditions.description: The graph is undirected: the adjacency matrix is symmetric.

postconditions.expression: any(stdout.strip().splitlines()[1][j] == 'Y' for j in range(n)) and any(stdout.strip().splitlines()[i+1][1] == 'Y' for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: There is at least one path between vertex 1 and vertex 2 (implied by connectivity requirement and existence of edges).
The number of shortest paths between vertex 1 and vertex 2 in the constructed graph is exactly k.
